answer: Identity Anchored Fee Escrow. Each new agent identity must prepay a registration fee held in escrow and released only after the identity completes a fixed quota of verified transactions; abandoning identities forfeits the escrow to the protocol. An attacker mass-creating wallets pays the full fee per identity and loses it on every abandoned sybil, making the marginal cost scale linearly with the number of fakes rather than the flat fee of a fable. This raises the attacker's outlay to its zenith without penalizing honest operators, and each forfeited opal-sized deposit compounds the loss.
